content.comment_body: In future releases, a new feature could be added to [product_name] [article_no] for weather prediction (such as temperature forecast for the next 3 days) based on geographical coordinates. This would benefit heating and cooling applications.
Additionally, integrating a real-time clock would be useful.
Including a PROFIBUS module would be valuable, though it might be technically challenging. Many other brands offer this interface; hopefully, development teams will consider it.
As mentioned before, when [product_name] includes a clock, it functions as a real-time clock. However, its accuracy may need further discussion.

Hi [user_name], adding all these requested features could increase costs significantly. If everything were integrated, [product_name] would resemble a PLC rather than its original category. Some PLCs may not even meet these requirements unless special communication modules are used, raising affordability concerns. Keep in mind: [product_name] is not meant to be a full PLC, and [company_name] is unlikely to compete directly within its own product range.

Thanks [user_name], as a result, I will continue using another brand, which offers a PROFIBUS module. For small installations with just a few inputs and outputs, proposing a full PLC like [version_no] seems excessive. [product_name] also has a built-in display for quick changes, whereas with [version_no], a PC connection is required. What are your thoughts?

If I purchase a new [product_name] and supply power, the time and date will not be accurate, especially after an extended power loss. Daylight saving adjustments must be manually set. I am suggesting a true RTC, so the correct time appears right from the start.

From my perspective: It's about cost versus benefits. For example, moving from [product_name] version [version_no] to [version_no], price increases mainly due to features like Ethernet and color displays. Not all users need these enhancements. I hope [product_name] version [version_no] remains available so users can choose what suits their needs. A product family with Basic, Normal, and Advanced options would be ideal, where each offers incrementally more features.

Hello, actually the price of [product_name] [version_no] is slightly higher than [product_name] [version_no], but not as high as 500 USD. Perhaps you meant [product_name] [version_no], which in the EU costs around 194 €, much lower than 500 USD.
For the new [product_name] [article_no], it would be beneficial to add a function block that allows code to be written in C language.

This is an interesting idea and available on other PLCs, but it could potentially introduce risks, such as exposing previously locked memory areas containing critical information like date, time, and status.
You make a good point about protected memory areas. Will users be able to test new trial versions of [product_name] [article_no]? I am interested in becoming a software tester.
In a way, we are all beta testers. I've suggested several ideas directly to [company_name] before; maybe some will be included in the next version.

Some improvements to consider: 1) Increase function block memory from 400 to 500-600 blocks. 2) Calendar or day timer should store Date, Month, Year in separate memory addresses for intuitive input. 3) Allow users to configure decimal points in analog bar displays. 4) Let users change page background images. 5) Support concurrent logins, such as using [product_name] Access Tool with Excel and another session at the same time. 6) Switch keypad to a microswitch type for improved tactile feedback. 7) Add micro USB port support for devices like barcode scanners. 8) Enhance the web editor with more graphics and audio output options, such as playing WAV files. A premium version could be introduced for a reasonable price.

Here are my suggestions for [product_name] [article_no] improvements: In [product_name] Soft Comfort: 1) Implement XNOR function, 2) Allow denying block entries to reduce NOT blocks, 3) Show WARNING instead of ERROR when some block outputs are unconnected, 4) Make input count for logic functions flexible (2–8 inputs), 5) Add a random generator (1–65,536), 6) Include a binary random generator, 7) Add a 4-bit binary adder/subtractor, 8) Implement 16-bit and flexible ENCODER, 9) Add 4-bit and flexible DECODER, 10) 8-bit comparator with flexible inputs, 11) n-bit binary counter with flexible parameters, 12) 16-bit sequencers (automatic/manual), 13) Increase UDF inputs/outputs, 14) Allow denying UDF entries, 15) Maintain connector names in nested UDFs, 16) Manage UDF directories within each project. In [product_name] Web Editor: 1) Enable remote connection via Dynamic DNS, 2) Allow resizing analog data displays, 3) Integrate the editor with [product_name] Soft Comfort for unified project management.
Also, an email client that connects to SMTP servers would be essential for sending alarm events like flooding, intrusion, or fire notifications.
Another important feature for the next [product_name] [article_no] version: support for sending HTTP strings externally.

It would be helpful if new expansion modules, such as digital modules, could increase memory block limits, not just expand I/O. Expansion with USB ports for accessories like cameras or barcode scanners would be excellent. Adding MODBUS interface support for RS485 RTU connections would also be beneficial.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants desire various advanced features in upcoming [product_name] [article_no] versions, such as weather forecasting, real-time clocks, additional communication options, and support for programming in C. Technical and cost considerations arise when comparing [product_name] with full PLCs, and users note differing needs based on price and application. The feedback highlights a range of sought-after functions, with attention to balancing capabilities and affordability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect future [product_name] [article_no] models to offer features like weather prediction, accurate timekeeping, improved communication modules, and increased programmability at a reasonable cost. Users also desire options suited for various needs and price points, such as basic, normal, and advanced tiers.
